reason: The cited docs page fully supports the trades-only aggregation and the missing bars, but it does not mention the Polygon.io rename. The rename is confirmed by Massive's own announcement (effective Oct 30, 2025), which the claim should cite.
found: Aggregates are derived exclusively from qualifying trades that meet specific conditions. If no eligible trades occur within a given timeframe, no aggregate bar is produced, resulting in an empty interval that indicates a lack of trading activity during that period.
suggested_fix: Massive (formerly Polygon.io; renamed October 2025, per https://massive.com/blog/polygon-is-now-massive) builds option aggregate bars only from qualifying trades, so intervals with no trade have no bar.

found: We use a slippage of 75% of bid ask width for single legs all the way to 53% for four leg spreads.

reason: The quoted range comes from a framing note that combines two FlashAlpha studies. The 7-year backtest provides only the honest-fill (breakeven-to-negative) numbers. The strongly positive mid-fill result comes from the companion study 'VRP Backtest: The Fill Model Is the Edge'. The note also says the setup is a single VRP short-put-spread strategy, 2019-2026, on five symbols.
found: A follow-up controlled study, VRP Backtest: The Fill Model Is the Edge , shows the result is bounded by the fill-model assumption : honest fills give breakeven to negative (these numbers); idealized mid-fills (the universal public-backtest default) give strongly positive.
suggested_fix: FlashAlpha's 7-year VRP short-put-spread backtest (2019-2026, five symbols) gives breakeven to negative results with honest fills; its companion fill-model study finds strongly positive results with idealized mid fills.
